es.summary: Lesión erosiva de la mucosa gástrica o duodenal causada principalmente por H. pylori o AINE. Produce dolor epigástrico y riesgo de sangrado.
key_points: Dolor típico entre comidas o nocturno
H. pylori y AINE son causas principales
Diagnóstico con pruebas de H. pylori y endoscopia
Tratamiento combina inhibidores de bomba de protones y antibióticos

pathophysiology: Infección por H. pylori altera la mucosa y aumenta la producción de ácido
AINE inhiben prostaglandinas, reduciendo la secreción de mucus protector
El exceso de ácido erosiona la barrera mucosa, formando la úlcera
Si la úlcera se profundiza, puede comprometer vasos sanguíneos y perforar
risk_factors: Estrés crónico y antecedentes familiares de úlcera
signs_symptoms: Dolor ardiente epigástrico, empeora en ayunas
Alivio temporal con alimentos o antiácidos
Melena o anemia por sangrado oculto
diagnostics: Prueba de aliento con urea: resultado positivo indica H. pylori
Test de antígeno en heces o serología para H. pylori
Endoscopia digestiva alta: visualiza úlcera y permite biopsia
Hemograma: Hb <12 g/dL sugiere sangrado; Hct <36 %
treatment: Inhibidor de bomba de protones (omeprazol, esomeprazol) para reducir ácido
Antagonista H2 (ranitidina, famotidina) si PPI no disponible
Terapia triple: PPI + amoxicilina + claritromicina (o metronidazol)
Sucralfato o misoprostol para proteger la mucosa
Endoscopia terapéutica si hay sangrado activo
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor usando escala 0‑10 y registrar patrón
Monitorear signos vitales y signos de sangrado (hematemesis, melena)
Controlar Hb y Hct cada 24‑48 h si hay sangrado
Administrar PPI y antibióticos según prescripción, observar efectos adversos
Mantener ayuno pre‑endoscopia y posición semisentada post‑procedimiento
patient_teaching: Evitar AINE, alcohol y tabaco durante y después del tratamiento
Tomar antibióticos completos aunque mejore el dolor
Tomar PPI antes de las comidas y no omitir dosis
Reportar vómitos con sangre o heces negras inmediatamente
Seguir dieta blanda y evitar alimentos picantes

outcomes: Control del dolor: dolor ≤3 en escala 0‑10
Paciente reporta alivio del dolor después de medicación

interventions.action: Evaluar dolor cada 2 h usando escala numérica
interventions.rationale: Permite medir efectividad del tratamiento y ajustar intervenciones

interventions.action: Administrar inhibidor de bomba de protones según orden
interventions.rationale: Reduce la secreción ácida y favorece la cicatrización

interventions.action: Ofrecer antiácido de acción rápida si el dolor es intenso
interventions.rationale: Alivia el dolor al neutralizar ácido temporalmente

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente semisentado para disminuir reflujo
interventions.rationale: Reduce irritación de la mucosa y mejora comodidad

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre evitar alimentos irritantes
interventions.rationale: Previene estímulo adicional del dolor

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
related_to: Infección por H. pylori con ulceración profunda
outcomes: Peso corporal estable, sin pérdida >2 % en 48 h

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y presión arterial cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta signos tempranos de hipovolemia

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos (I/O)
interventions.rationale: Evalúa balance hídrico y detecta pérdidas ocultas

interventions.action: Observar sangre en vómitos o heces y notificar al médico
interventions.rationale: Identifica hemorragia que puede causar déficit de volumen

interventions.action: Administrar solución intravenosa según indicación si hay sangrado
interventions.rationale: Restituye volumen intravascular y previene shock

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de deshidratación y sangrado
interventions.rationale: Promueve detección temprana y búsqueda de ayuda

en.summary: Erosive lesion of the gastric or duodenal mucosa primarily caused by H. pylori or NSAIDs. Produces epigastric pain and risk of bleeding.
key_points: Typical pain between meals or at night
H. pylori and NSAIDs are main causes
Diagnosis with H. pylori tests and endoscopy
Treatment combines proton pump inhibitors and antibiotics

pathophysiology: H. pylori infection alters mucosa and increases acid production
NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandins, reducing protective mucus secretion
Excess acid erodes mucosal barrier, forming ulcer
If ulcer deepens, it can compromise blood vessels and perforate
risk_factors: Chronic stress and family history of ulcer
signs_symptoms: Burning epigastric pain, worse on an empty stomach
Temporary relief with food or antacids
Melena or anemia from occult bleeding
diagnostics: Urea breath test: positive result indicates H. pylori
Stool antigen test or serology for H. pylori
Upper endoscopy: visualizes ulcer and allows biopsy
CBC: Hb <12 g/dL suggests bleeding; Hct <36 %
treatment: Proton pump inhibitor (omeprazole, esomeprazole) to reduce acid
H2 antagonist (ranitidine, famotidine) if PPI unavailable
Triple therapy: PPI + amoxicillin + clarithromycin (or metronidazole)
Sucralfate or misoprostol to protect mucosa
nursing_care: Assess pain using 0‑10 scale and record pattern
Monitor vital signs and signs of bleeding (hematemesis, melena)
Check Hb and Hct every 24‑48 h if bleeding
Administer PPI and antibiotics per order, observe adverse effects
Maintain pre‑endoscopy fasting and semirecumbent position post‑procedure
patient_teaching: Avoid NSAIDs, alcohol, and tobacco during and after treatment
Take full course of antibiotics even if pain improves
Take PPI before meals and do not miss doses
Report vomiting with blood or black stools immediately
Follow a bland diet and avoid spicy foods

outcomes: Patient reports pain relief after medication

interventions.action: Assess pain every 2 h using numeric scale
interventions.rationale: Measures treatment effectiveness and guides adjustments

interventions.action: Administer proton pump inhibitor as ordered
interventions.rationale: Reduces acid secretion and promotes healing

interventions.action: Offer rapid‑acting antacid if pain is intense
interventions.rationale: Alleviates pain by temporarily neutralizing acid

interventions.action: Position patient semirecumbent to reduce reflux
interventions.rationale: Decreases mucosal irritation and improves comfort

interventions.action: Educate patient about avoiding irritating foods
interventions.rationale: Prevents additional pain stimulus

related_to: H. pylori infection with deep ulceration
outcomes: Stable body weight, no loss >2 % in 48 h

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and blood pressure every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early signs of hypovolemia

interventions.action: Record intake and output (I/O)
interventions.rationale: Assesses fluid balance and detects hidden losses

interventions.action: Observe blood in vomitus or stool and notify physician
interventions.rationale: Identifies bleeding that may cause volume deficit

interventions.action: Administer IV fluid as indicated if bleeding
interventions.rationale: Restores intravascular volume and prevents shock

interventions.action: Educate patient on signs of dehydration and bleeding
interventions.rationale: Promotes early detection and seeking help

summary.1.quote: The most common cause is infection with a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori . Another cause is the long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs) such as aspirin and ibuprofen.

key_points.0.quote: The pain: Starts between meals or during the night

key_points.1.quote: The most common cause is infection with a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori . Another cause is the long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs) such as aspirin and ibuprofen.

key_points.2.quote: pylori infection, your doctor will test your blood, breath, or stool. Your doctor also may look inside your stomach and duodenum by doing an endoscopy or x-ray.

key_points.3.quote: Treatment may include medicines to reduce stomach acids or antibiotics to kill H. pylori.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Peptic ulcers happen when the acids that help you digest food damage the walls of the stomach or duodenum.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Another cause is the long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs) such as aspirin and ibuprofen.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Not smoking and avoiding alcohol can help.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: A burning stomach pain is the most common symptom.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Briefly stops if you eat or take antacids

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Common assessment findings for patients with acute GI bleeding are: abdominal pain or cramping anemia cool, clammy skin decreased LOC decreased urine output hematemesis (bloody vomitus) hypoactive bowel sounds hypotension melena (bloody stools) and/or dark tarry stools tachycardia

sections.treatment.0.quote: Most patients experiencing bleeding from stress ulcers will also be recommended to take a PPI such as omeprazole (e.g., Prilosec) or pantoprazole (Protonix) to decrease gastric acid secretion and allow for complete healing of the ulcer.

sections.treatment.4.quote: If an acute GI bleed is suspected, the patient will likely be scheduled for an emergent endoscopy.

sections.complications.0.quote: Common assessment findings for patients with acute GI bleeding are: abdominal pain or cramping anemia cool, clammy skin decreased LOC decreased urine output hematemesis (bloody vomitus) hypoactive bowel sounds hypotension melena (bloody stools) and/or dark tarry stools tachycardia

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: It is important for the nurse to closely monitor the patient’s hemodynamic status and vital signs and intervene as needed.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Most patients experiencing bleeding from stress ulcers will also be recommended to take a PPI such as omeprazole (e.g., Prilosec) or pantoprazole (Protonix) to decrease gastric acid secretion and allow for complete healing of the ulcer.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Another cause is the long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs) such as aspirin and ibuprofen.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Patients are prescribed a2-week course of antibiotics to eradicate the bacteria completely and prevent the development of additional ulcers in the future.
